test_title: SSC Selection Post 2024 (Higher Secondary Level) Official Paper (Held On: 20 Jun, 2024 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Which of the following statements is INCORRECT according to the passage?

options.text: The RBI and commercial banks annually spend around Rupees 21,000 crore in currency operations costs.
Citizens of Delhi alone spend Rupees 9.1 crore and 60 lakh hours in collecting cash.
Less than 4% of our population pays income tax.
Payments by mobiles have grown from 860 transactions in 2010 to 4.4 million in 2014.

solution:
The correct answer is '**Less than 4% of our population pays income tax**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The passage explicitly states, "**Given that less than three per cent of our population pays income tax**," not less than 4%.
 
• All other statistics related to currency operations costs, the time and money spent by citizens, and the growth of mobile payments are mentioned accurately.
 
• A correct understanding of percentages is crucial in this context since even a small numerical difference can significantly change the meaning.
 
• The detail about the percentage of the population paying income tax is specific and does not match option 3.

Therefore, the correct answer is ‘**Option 3**’.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The RBI and commercial banks annually spend around Rupees 21,000 crore in currency operations costs:**

 
 
• This figure is directly mentioned in the passage: "The RBI and commercial banks annually spend around Rupees 21,000 crore in currency operations costs."
 
 
 
• **Citizens of Delhi alone spend Rupees 9.1 crore and 60 lakh hours in collecting cash:**
 
 
• This expenditure and time spent are specified in the passage: "while the citizens of Delhi alone spend Rupees 9.1 crore and 60 lakh hours in collecting cash."
 
 
 
• **Payments by mobiles have grown from 860 transactions in 2010 to 4.4 million in 2014:**
 
 
• The passage confirms this information: "payments by mobiles have grown from just 860 transactions in November 2010 to 4.4 million in August 2014."
